# Wayne Hendricks

> HPC engineer who builds supercomputers and the training infrastructure behind
> foundation models. Founding HPC engineer at Paige.AI from 2018 through its $81M
> acquisition by Tempus in 2025, where he built the GPU, storage, and scheduling
> infrastructure behind the Virchow and PRISM pathology foundation models and the
> company's FDA-cleared diagnostic products. Previously principal administrator of
> the Caltech CMS Tier-2 for the Large Hadron Collider. Based in New York City.
> Contact: twh@waynehendricks.com

## Current role

Senior HPC Engineer at Tempus AI (New York City), 2018–present, continuing through
the September 2025 acquisition of Paige.AI. Runs GPU systems on GCP for
clinical-grade computational pathology models and is migrating the Paige Azure
training stack into Tempus's GCP environment.

## Systems built

- **Azul** (Paige.AI, 2022–2025). Scalable Azure CycleCloud and Slurm cluster,
  hundreds of GPUs, 7 PB of multi-modal data on tiered storage, 1.5M jobs run in
  2025. The production training environment behind Virchow, Virchow2, PRISM,
  PRISM2, and OmniScreen.
- **Pathfinder** (Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center, 2018–2022). On-prem
  NVIDIA DGX-1 Volta AI/ML cluster, 100 GPUs, 5 PB of pathology images in tiered
  storage. The first DGX-1 Volta cluster at a cancer center, a collaboration
  between the Fuchs Lab and its spinoff, Paige.
- **CMST2** (Caltech High Energy Physics, 2015–2018). 7,300-slot HTCondor cluster
  with 4.5 PB of physics collision data. One of the seven major U.S. Tier-2 sites
  on the Worldwide LHC Computing Grid and the Open Science Grid, the world's
  largest distributed computing grid.

## Expertise

GPU cluster architecture across NVIDIA Pascal, Volta, Ampere, Hopper, and
Blackwell. Slurm, Azure CycleCloud, HTCondor, Kueue, and Kubernetes for scheduling
and orchestration. InfiniBand, RoCE, NVLink/NVSwitch, GPUDirect RDMA, NCCL, and
DOCA for high-performance fabrics. Lustre, Weka, GPFS, NetApp, Pure, and S3/Blob
for high performance storage and data archival at petabyte scale. Azure, AWS, and
GCP with Terraform, Packer, and Ansible. Network performance and systems debugging
on Linux, and automation with mostly shell and Python.

Supports and debugs the full training and inference stack that ML researchers run
on these systems, including PyTorch (DDP and FSDP), distributed checkpointing and
checkpoint resharding, Ray, Dask, Prefect, NeMo, Megatron, Triton, and vLLM, along
with CUDA, NCCL, and the collective-communication and fabric layers underneath
them. Day-to-day debugging with strace, ltrace, perf, sysdig, lsof, dtrace, and
eBPF/bpftrace. Earlier infrastructure work spans Ceph, ZFS, Gluster, VMware, KVM,
OpenStack, Puppet, Salt, Nagios, Ganglia, InfluxDB, DataDog, PagerDuty, SSSD,
OpenLDAP, Okta, CIS hardening, FreeBSD, Solaris, Perl, and Ruby.

Two decades of systems and network engineering underneath the AI work: TCP/IP with
nmap, Wireshark, and tcpdump; network topology design across Mellanox, Arista,
Cisco NX-OS/IOS, Dell Force10, and EdgeCore whitebox switching; security and
identity with iptables, BSD Packet Filter, Nessus, hostapd, Shibboleth, SSSD,
OpenLDAP, Okta, and SentinelOne; enterprise monitoring with RRDtool, Cacti,
Nagios, HP OpenView, CA Spectrum, ServiceNow, and Tableau; web and application
infrastructure with Apache, NGINX, Squid, Java/WebLogic, and Jekyll; OpenMPI and
high throughput computing; bare metal provisioning, hardware procurement, budget
management, datacenter acquisition, change and incident management, and 24/7 NOC
operations. Also does technical interviewing and engineering hiring from
individual contributor through VP level.

## Publications

Credited for infrastructure contributions on the Virchow pathology foundation
model (Nature Medicine, 2024) and its successors Virchow2, PRISM, PRISM2, and
OmniScreen, and on the INDIS '15 / SC15 software-defined networking work.
Co-author on two CHEP 2016 papers in Journal of Physics: Conference Series
(SDN-NGenIA; HTTP as a Data Access Protocol: Trials with XrootD in CMS's AAA
Project).
